sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: CI/CD interview questions cover the pipelines that ship every modern Java backend — GitHub Actions vs Jenkins vs GitLab CI, declarative Jenkins pipelines, secret management, deployment strategies (blue/green, canary, rolling, feature flags), trunk-based development, automated rollback on SLO regression, and the production debugging questions interviewers love ("the pipeline is suddenly 4x slower — what now?"). For Terraform/IaC questions, see the dedicated Terraform page; for Jenkins-specific deep dives, see the Jenkins page.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
CI ≠ CD ≠ CDeployment. Always disambiguate.

- **CI** — every commit builds + tests on the trunk.
- **Continuous Delivery** — every passing build is releasable.
- **Continuous Deployment** — every passing build *is* released.
- **Pipeline** stages: build → test → security scan → package → deploy → smoke → monitor.
- **Rollback** is a feature, not an afterthought.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Cicd fundamentals** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Comparisons** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Deployment strategies** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Github actions** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Rollback strategies** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Blue/green vs canary** — full-cutover vs progressive; pick by blast radius tolerance.
- **Feature flags** > long-lived branches; merge quickly, expose progressively.
- **Secrets** in CI — short-lived OIDC tokens > static keys.
- **Pipeline as code** — Jenkinsfile / `.github/workflows`; review in PR.
- **SLO-based deploy** — auto-rollback on regression; the modern target.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd run trunk-based with PR builds, deploy on merge to staging, gate prod on a manual approval (or auto-promote on green SLOs), use canary + auto-rollback, and feature-flag risky changes so deploys are decoupled from releases."*
